learning_outcomes.text: Have knowledge and understanding of the basic concepts of production and logistics planning and control.
Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering by applying knowledge of mathematics, statistics, economics, and other scientific fields to the analysis of business situations.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve industrial organization engineering problems using established methods.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to the analysis of process and methods engineering.
Be able to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out the design and management of production and logistics systems and the design of industrial processes.
Be able to select and use appropriate tools and methods applicable in industrial organization.
Be aware of all implications of engineering practice.
Demonstrate awareness of business and project management practices, as well as risk management and control, and understand their limitations.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to the analysis of product, process, and methods engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs that meet specific requirements.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods.
Awareness of all implications of engineering practice.
Demonstrate awareness of business and project management practices, as well as risk management and control, and understand their limitations.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component, or process in the field of mechanical engineering, to meet required specifications.
Applied knowledge of business organization.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to operations, production, and the supply chain
Qualitative and quantitative techniques and tools applicable to industrial business organization
Demand forecasting and inventory management. Warehouse management
Independent demand inventory management models. Batches
Warehouse management. Full cycle: Reception, storage, picking, dispatch. Information Systems
Production and logistics planning and control. MRP
Material Requirements Planning (MRP). Master program. Demand explosion and anticipation
teaching_methods: Student work and case discussion in class

assessment_methods.method: Other evaluation components (e.g., partial exams, continuous assessment)

assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of 60% from the final exam and 40% from the rest of the evaluation components. Partial exams will be held throughout the course. Optionally, complementary evaluation systems may be used, with possible sampling correction. A minimum grade of 4 is required in the final exam to pass the course. The final evaluation will be carried out through a written final exam that will globally assess the knowledge, skills, and abilities acquired.
